footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income to W. P. Carey: after $6.6M attributable to noncontrolling interests. The data provider reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow. Operating income follows StockAnalysis, which places unusual items below the operating line: −$2.2M merger & restructuring charges, −$70.4M asset writedowns, −$103M gains/losses on investments, $194M gains/losses on asset sales in 2025; −$4.5M merger & restructuring charges, −$43.6M asset writedowns, −$102M gains/losses on investments, $74.8M gains/losses on asset sales, $10.7M other unusual items in 2024 (signs as reported: negative = charge).

Figures are from StockAnalysis (S&P Global Market Intelligence data) for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier; free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items not reported there are left out.
Diluted EPS by quarter as reported in the 10-Qs; fourth quarters are calculated (net income ÷ estimated diluted shares) because EPS does not add across quarters.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: W. P. Carey is a REIT that owns industrial, warehouse and retail properties net-leased to companies. Revenue rose 8.2% to $1.7B in 2025. Operating income rose 11.7% to $890M, a 52.2% margin.
Net income rose 1.2% to $466M, or $2.11 per share. Operating cash flow was $1.3B and free cash flow $1.3B, versus $1.8B; W. P. Carey returned $805M through dividends and buybacks.
